h2: Pool Equipment Jimbaran – Pumps, Filters & Chlorinators
intro: Salt air off the bay, hard water from the Bukit aquifer, and villas stacked up the hillside all put extra strain on pool equipment in Jimbaran. Whether your pump keeps losing prime, a multiport valve is weeping, or the chlorinator cell has gone white with scale, Bali Fix handles installation and repair across Jimbaran Bay, Bukit Jimbaran, and surrounding neighbourhoods.

sections.h3: How Jimbaran's Conditions Wear Down Your Pool Gear
sections.text: Salt-laden air near the bay corrodes fittings, impellers, and electrical terminals faster than inland. Up in Bukit Jimbaran and Goa Gong, low tank pressure makes pumps cycle on and off, while hard water deposits scale inside heaters, mixers, and filter housings. These three forces shorten the life of every component—from cartridge filters to auto-fill valves—so regular attention matters more here than in flat, dry areas.

sections.h3: Common Repairs We Handle Around Kedonganan & Jimbaran Bay
sections.text: A pump that hums but won't turn after a power cut, a sand filter shedding grit into the basin, a multiport handle leaking at the stem, or a salt chlorinator producing no chlorine—these are the calls we see most often in larger family villas. Flickering or dead pool lights usually trace back to corroded terminals rather than the bulb itself. Send a short clip of the issue and we'll point you toward the right fix before it grows.

sections.h3: What to Send on WhatsApp for a Quick Quote
sections.text: A clear photo of the equipment label (brand, model, size) plus a ten-second video showing the problem saves us both time. For filters, include a shot of the sand level or cartridge condition; for pumps, note whether it runs hot, grinds, or simply won't prime. Pricing depends entirely on the specific job and parts involved, so once we've seen what you sent, we can give you an honest figure over WhatsApp without guesswork.

sections.h3: Prevention Tips for Bay-Side and Hillside Pools
sections.text: Rinse exposed fittings and pump housings with fresh water every couple of weeks if your villa sits near the bay—the chloride film accelerates corrosion even under a cover. In hillside properties, check that your tank float valve isn't stuck, because constant low pressure forces the pool pump to work harder than designed. Backwash your sand filter on schedule rather than waiting for pressure to spike, and wipe chlorinator cells clean each season to keep scale from building up in hard-water conditions.

faq.q: Does salt air really damage pool equipment this quickly?
faq.a: Yes—near the bay, chloride ions settle on metal parts and electrical terminals, eating through protective coatings within months. A simple freshwater rinse every two weeks slows the process noticeably.

faq.q: My pump keeps cycling on and off. Is it broken?
faq.a: Not necessarily. On hillside villas, low tank pressure or a partially blocked suction line makes the pump lose prime repeatedly. We can tell whether it's a pressure issue or an internal seal problem once you send us a short video.

faq.q: How do I know when my filter sand needs replacing?
faq.a: It depends on usage and local water quality, but if backwashing stops restoring flow or fine grit starts showing up in the pool, the sand has likely broken down and a full change is due.
